glosses: A disguise or covering up.
The act of disguising.
The use of natural or artificial material on personnel, objects, or tactical positions with the aim of confusing, misleading, or evading the enemy.
A pattern on clothing consisting of irregularly shaped patches that are either greenish/brownish, brownish/whitish, or bluish/whitish, as used by ground combat forces.
The resemblance of an organism to its surroundings for avoiding detection.

examples.text: Earless ghost swift moths become “invisible” to echolocating bats by forming mating clusters close[…]above vegetation and effectively blending into the clutter of echoes that the bat receives from the leaves and stems around them. Many insects probably use this strategy, which is a close analogy to crypsis in the visible world—camouflage and other methods for blending into one’s visual background.

glosses: Clothes made from camouflage fabric, for concealment in combat or hunting.
To hide or disguise something by covering it up or changing its appearance.

examples.text:
THE CONCISE ENCYCLOPAEDIA OF WORLD RAILWAY LOCOMOTIVES. Edited by P. Ransome-Wallis. Hutchinson. 50s.
A gaudy jacket, remarkably out of keeping with the contents, camouflages the weightiest and meatiest work on a railway topic since the war.

Elegant brick and stone buildings, with iron and glass canopies and decorative wooden scalloping and fencing—all evidencing care on the part of the architect to produce a pleasing, well-planned building—were submerged beneath a profusion of ill-conceived additions and camouflaged by vulgar paint schemes; and the original conception was lost.

glosses: A lid.
Area or situation which screens a person or thing from view.

examples.text: The soldiers took cover behind a ruined building.

glosses: The front and back of a book, magazine, CD package, etc.
The top sheet of a bed.
A cloth or similar material, often fitted, placed over an item such as a car or sofa or food to protect it from dust, rain, insects, etc. when not being used.
A cover charge.

examples.text: There's a $15 cover tonight.

glosses: A setting at a restaurant table or formal dinner.

examples.text: We need to set another cover for the Smith party.

glosses: A new performance or rerecording of a previously recorded song; a cover version; a cover song.
A fielding position on the off side, between point and mid off, about 30° forward of square; a fielder in this position.

examples.text: The captain signalled his best fielder from short leg to cover.

glosses: A tarpaulin or other device used to cover the wicket during rain, to prevent it getting wet.

examples.text: The covers were put on just before lunch.

glosses: The area of the stumps that is blocked by the batsman so as to defend the wicket.
A backup incase any player sustains injury during nets or midseries. Originally have to be declared part of squad before match.

examples.text: He was brought in as cover for wicketkeeper.

glosses: A collection (or family) of subsets of a given set, whose union contains every element of said original set.

examples.text: The open intervals are a cover for the real numbers.

glosses: An envelope complete with stamps and postmarks etc.
A solid object, including terrain, that provides protection from enemy fire.

In commercial law, a buyer’s purchase on the open market of goods similar or identical to the goods contracted for after a seller has breached a contract of sale by failure to deliver the goods contracted for.
An insurance contract; coverage by an insurance contract.
A persona maintained by a spy or undercover operative; cover story.
A swindler's confederate.
The portion of a slate, tile, or shingle that is hidden by the overlap of the course above.
In a steam engine, the lap of a slide valve.
The distance between reinforcing steel and the exterior of concrete.
Of or pertaining to the front cover of a book or magazine.
Of, pertaining to, or consisting of cover versions.
To place something over or upon, as to conceal or protect.

examples.text: He covered the baby with a blanket.
When the pot comes to a boil, cover it and reduce the heat to medium.

glosses: To be over or upon, as to conceal or protect.

examples.text: The blanket covered the baby.

glosses: To have under one’s scope or purview.
To deal with or include someone or something.

examples.text: Richard Morgan covers science for The Economist, The New York Times, Scientific American, and Wired.

glosses: To have under one’s scope or purview.

glosses: To have under one’s scope or purview.

glosses: To be enough money for.

examples.text: Dad, when I get to University, will I be covered?

glosses: To act as a replacement.

examples.text: I need to take off Tuesday. Can you cover for me?

glosses: To air or run locally originated material in place of network material during an internal spot break in a syndicated program.

examples.text: I wish that popular afternoon show would let us cover some of their commercials – their national stuff can be so annoying.

glosses: To make a cover version of (a song that was originally recorded by another artist).

examples.text: I'm surprised that the band covered this Beatles song so well.
